title: Zscaler to Splunk Onboarding Reference

overview.description: All web/HTTP(S) traffic processed by the ZIA proxy — URL, user, category, action, bytes.
overview.input_method: NSS feed (syslog→SC4S) or Cloud NSS (HTTPS push→Splunk HEC)
overview.configuration_settings:
ZIA Admin Portal > Administration > Nanolog Streaming Service:
• NSS Server (VM) provisioned and paired to a ZIA Public Service Edge
• NSS Feed: type=Web; SIEM IP/FQDN + port (SC4S host:514 by default); TCP or SSL/TLS transport
• Feed output format: default or custom %s{field} template; escape character; duplicate-log/rate-limit option
• Filters: log type, user/dept/location, action (optional)
Cloud NSS alternative: destination = Splunk HEC URL; HEC token; JSON output; batch interval
Splunk/SC4S side: listener on 514/tcp (or HEC port 8088); sourcetype override to zscalernss-web; index=netproxy

overview.description: Non-web traffic (any port/protocol) processed by the ZIA cloud firewall — src/dst IP, port, protocol, rule.
overview.input_method: NSS feed (syslog→SC4S) or Cloud NSS (HTTPS push→Splunk HEC)
overview.configuration_settings:
Same NSS Server/VM as Web feed, separate NSS Feed object:
• NSS Feed: type=Firewall; SIEM IP/FQDN + port; TCP/SSL transport
• Custom feed format must append \tvendor=Zscaler\tproduct=fw before the newline so SC4S auto-detects the sourcetype
• Filters: aggregate vs. session logs, action (allow/block), IPS/threat-only
Splunk/SC4S side: sourcetype override zscalernss-fw; index=netfw

overview.description: DNS queries/responses routed through Zscaler — queried domain, resolved IP, policy action.
overview.input_method: NSS feed (syslog→SC4S) or Cloud NSS (HTTPS push→Splunk HEC)
overview.configuration_settings:
• NSS Feed: type=DNS; SIEM IP/FQDN + port; TCP/SSL transport
• Custom feed format must append \tvendor=Zscaler\tproduct=dns before the newline for SC4S auto-detection
• Filters: request vs. response logs, category
Splunk/SC4S side: sourcetype override zscalernss-dns; index=netdns

overview.description: GRE/IPSec tunnel lifecycle events between customer edge and Zscaler — up/down, aggregate traffic stats.
overview.configuration_settings:
• NSS Feed: type=Tunnel; SIEM IP/FQDN + port; TCP/SSL transport
• No Cloud NSS/HEC option in most deployments — syslog only
Splunk/SC4S side: sourcetype override zscalernss-tunnel; index=netops

overview.description: Operational/system alerts from the ZIA cloud platform itself (service issues), not user traffic.
overview.configuration_settings:
• NSS Feed: type=Alert (built on the Web NSS format); SIEM IP/FQDN + port
• Custom feed format must append \tvendor=Zscaler\tproduct=alerts before the newline for SC4S auto-detection
Splunk/SC4S side: sourcetype override zscalernss-alerts; index=main

overview.description: Administrative activity in the ZIA Admin Portal — who changed what policy/config, and when.
overview.configuration_settings:
• API credentials: OAuth2 client via ZIdentity (Client ID, Client Secret, Vanity/Customer Domain) on newer tenants, or legacy ZIA API Key + Admin Username + Password on tenants not yet migrated
• Base/cloud URL for the ZIA tenant (e.g. https://admin.<cloud>.zscaler.net or the ZIdentity token endpoint)
• Splunk TA input: polling interval, checkpoint (last record id/timestamp), proxy settings if egress is restricted
• TLS certificate validation for outbound HTTPS calls

overview.description: Full post-detonation malware analysis for files flagged by ZIA Sandbox — behavior, verdict, hashes.
overview.configuration_settings:
• Same API credential set as Admin Audit (OAuth2/ZIdentity or legacy API Key + Username + Password)
• Sandbox Report API is called per file hash after a sandbox verdict fires — mind published request-rate quotas
• Splunk TA input: polling interval; report detail level (summary vs. full)

overview.description: Every application access attempt through ZPA — user, app segment, connector used, session outcome/timings. (Zscaler calls this the “User Activity” log.)
overview.input_method: LSS — JSON stream over TLS, pushed from ZPA to a log receiver
overview.configuration_settings:
ZPA Admin Portal > Configuration & Control > Log Streaming Service > Add Log Receiver:
• App Connector Group(s) in scope
• Log Type = User Activity
• Session/Policy filter (optional)
• TLS certificate for the receiver; destination host:port (Splunk-side listener or SC4S)
• Output format = JSON

overview.description: User authentication/session status for ZPA — IdP used, SAML attributes, posture check results, session state. (Zscaler calls this the “User Status” log.)
overview.configuration_settings:
Same LSS Log Receiver mechanism as App Access, with:
• Log Type = User Status
• App Connector Group scope, TLS cert, destination host:port, JSON format

overview.description: Health/status of ZPA App Connectors — CPU/memory, interface stats, session state, connectivity to Service Edge.
overview.configuration_settings:
Same LSS Log Receiver mechanism, with:
• Log Type = App Connector Status
• App Connector Group scope, TLS cert, destination host:port, JSON format

overview.description: Access to internal apps via ZPA's clientless Browser Access feature — CORS/connection timing detail.
overview.configuration_settings:
Same LSS Log Receiver mechanism, with:
• Log Type = Browser Access
• App Connector Group scope, TLS cert, destination host:port, JSON format

overview.description: Inline threat-inspection results for private app traffic (ZPA AppProtection) — detected attacks/signatures.
overview.input_method: LSS — JSON stream over TLS (where available) or embedded in User Activity logs
overview.configuration_settings:
• Requires AppProtection enabled on the relevant Access Policy / app segments
• LSS Log Receiver (if your ZPA tenant exposes it as a distinct Log Type) with same TLS/host:port/JSON settings
NOTE: not independently documented as a distinct LSS log type in current public Zscaler/vendor field references — verify in your own ZPA Admin Portal's Log Streaming Service > Log Type list before building this input.

overview.description: Administrative activity in the ZPA Admin Portal — object created/changed/deleted, old/new values, admin session.
overview.configuration_settings:
Same LSS Log Receiver mechanism, with:
• Log Type = Audit
• App Connector Group scope, TLS cert, destination host:port, JSON format

overview.description: Enrichment/lookup data, NOT event logs — periodic snapshot of ZIA policy/config objects (e.g. URL category tables) used to enrich other events.
overview.sourcetype: n/a (lookup / KV store, not a log sourcetype)
overview.configuration_settings:
• API credentials: ZIA OAuth2/ZIdentity client or legacy API key
• Polling interval for each config object type
• Unofficial add-on — not supported by Zscaler; review its GitHub docs before deploying

overview.input: ZPA config objects (app segments, segment groups)
overview.description: Enrichment/lookup data, NOT event logs — periodic snapshot of ZPA app segment/segment group definitions.
overview.sourcetype: n/a (lookup / KV store, not a log sourcetype)
overview.configuration_settings:
• API credentials: ZPA OAuth2/ZIdentity client or legacy API key + secret
• Polling interval for each config object type
• Unofficial add-on — not supported by Zscaler; review its GitHub docs before deploying

overview_notes: Note: rows for ZDX, ZCC (Client Connector), CASB/SaaS Security, and DLP-incident REST inputs are intentionally omitted — not confirmed as part of the official Zscaler Technical Add-on for Splunk in current public documentation. Field names below are drawn from Zscaler's own NSS format reference (Web log) and from vendor integration docs (Elastic) for the other log types, since several official Zscaler field-reference pages are JavaScript-rendered and could not be scraped directly — verify exact field names against your own onboarded data before building dashboards/CIM mappings.

Web / Proxy logs (ZIA).source_reference: Zscaler Help Portal — NSS Feed Output Format: Web Logs (official %s{field} tokens; some low-signal duplicate/rarely-used fields grouped for readability). NOTE: the actual Zscaler Technical Add-on for Splunk (confirmed from its real props.conf, v4.1.5) extracts several of these under different internal names, e.g. reqmethod->requestmethod, ua->useragent, urlcat->urlcategory, threatcat->threatcategory, filename stays filename, md5 for file hash. See the CIM Field Mapping tab for the TA's confirmed internal field names.

Web Inspection / AppProtection logs (ZPA.source_reference: Not independently verifiable from current public Zscaler/vendor documentation — flagged rather than guessed.

fields.description: Elastic's current ZPA integration documents only five LSS log types — App Connector Status, Audit, Browser Access, User Activity, and User Status — with no separate AppProtection/Web Inspection field list. AppProtection detections may surface as attributes within the User Activity (App Access) log rather than as a standalone feed. Confirm the exact field set against your own ZPA Admin Portal > Log Streaming Service > Log Type options and a sample of onboarded data before building parsers/CIM mappings for this source.

cim_field_mapping_notes: Source: every row above is read directly from the real Zscaler Technical Add-on for Splunk package (Splunkbase app 3865, app ID TA-Zscaler_CIM, version 4.1.5) that the user provided — specifically its default/props.conf FIELDALIAS and EVAL stanzas. This is the exact shipped configuration, not an inferred or conventional mapping, and it supersedes every earlier version of this table. A few things worth internalizing: (1) EVAL directives run after FIELDALIAS and win when both target the same field name — several 'app' fields across ZPA sourcetypes are FIELDALIASed from a real value and then immediately overwritten by a hardcoded EVAL-app="Zscaler" literal, so 'app' is not useful for distinguishing ZPA applications in this TA version; (2) some CIM fields (category, signature) receive two competing FIELDALIAS sources on the same sourcetype (zscalernss-web's threatcategory/urlcategory and threatname/dlpdictionaries) — whichever stanza Splunk evaluates last for a given event wins, which is the root cause of a documented Splunk Community bug; (3) rows marked '— not tagged —' have real, working field aliases but are NOT wired into any CIM data model in this package version, so they will not appear in `| datamodel` searches no matter how CIM-like their field names look. If you're on a different TA version, diff your own props.conf/eventtypes.conf/tags.conf against this table before trusting it verbatim.
